questions.q: What does env.reset() return in the Gymnasium API?
options: Only the first observation
The first observation and an info dict
The final reward of the previous episode
The action space definition
questions.explain: reset() starts a new episode and returns a tuple of (observation, info).

questions.q: Why does step() return both terminated and truncated instead of a single done flag?
options: They mean the same thing, split only for backward compatibility
truncated is only used in vectorized environments
They distinguish a true end of episode from the environment's dynamics versus an external cutoff like a time limit
terminated applies to continuous spaces and truncated applies to discrete spaces
questions.explain: terminated signals the environment itself ended the episode (e.g. goal reached, agent died); truncated signals an external limit cut it off even though the task could have continued. Conflating them produces wrong value estimates near time limits.

questions.q: What is the correct use of the info dict returned by step()?
options: Feed it into the policy network alongside the observation
Use it for diagnostics and logging only, never for action selection
It replaces the reward signal in sparse-reward tasks
It must be identical in shape to observation_space
questions.explain: info holds diagnostic data outside the formal observation/reward contract. A policy that depends on it is effectively getting extra observation data through an undeclared side channel.

questions.q: spaces.Discrete(4) describes what kind of action or observation?
options: A continuous 4-dimensional vector bounded between fixed limits
One of 4 integer values, 0 through 3
A 4x4 image
A dictionary with 4 named fields
questions.explain: Discrete(n) represents one of n integers (0 to n-1), used for things like a fixed set of actions.

questions.q: Why do Gymnasium environments declare observation_space and action_space up front?
options: It is required only for rendering
So generic RL code, like a network's input layer or an action sampler, can be written once and reused across any environment with the same space types
It has no practical effect, it's purely documentation
To disable the render() method
questions.explain: Declaring spaces lets algorithm code stay environment-agnostic — the same policy architecture or action sampler works against any environment exposing compatible spaces.
